title: Cross-tenant data read via unscoped export lookup
description: The export download handler authenticates the caller but does not scope the export lookup to the caller's tenant, so any member can read another tenant's export by id.
root_cause: Lookup by export id omits the tenant predicate present on every other read path.
intended_behavior: An export is readable only by members of the tenant that owns it.

trace.description: Authenticated route; auth middleware runs but no ownership check follows.
Handler passes the raw id to the repository with no tenant argument.
Query selects the export by id only, with no tenant_id predicate.

evidence.description: Auth middleware present; no ownership or tenant check before the lookup.
SELECT filters on id alone, unlike sibling reads which include tenant_id.

conditions.description: Caller is any authenticated member of any tenant.
Caller knows or guesses an export id belonging to another tenant.

execution.attacker_perspective: An ordinary logged-in member of tenant A with no special role.
payloads: GET /api/v1/exports/<id owned by tenant B> with a valid tenant-A session cookie.
instructions: In a dummy-tenant integration test, seed one export for tenant B, authenticate as a tenant-A member, and request tenant B's export id.
execution.observed_result: Tenant A received tenant B's export body with HTTP 200 instead of 404 in the dummy-tenant integration test.

remediation.strategy: Scope the lookup to the caller's tenant at the last trusted decision point so a non-owning caller receives 404, matching the sibling read paths.

likelihood.reason: Any member can do it with a guessable or enumerable id.

confidence.reason: Complete source trace plus a reproduced dummy-tenant result.

title: Possible SSRF via member-set webhook URL
description: Members can set a webhook URL the server later fetches. Source does not show whether the egress proxy blocks internal ranges, so the decisive fact is outside the repository.
claimed_root_cause: A member-controlled webhook URL is fetched server-side with no source-visible internal-range block.

trace.description: Member sets an arbitrary webhook URL, stored without an allowlist.
Dispatcher fetches the stored URL directly.

evidence.description: Direct server-side fetch of the stored URL with no allowlist or internal-range check in source.

blockers: Whether the deployment egress proxy blocks link-local and private ranges is not present in the repository.

validation_plan.local: In the sandbox with an isolated loopback, point the webhook at a local dummy server and confirm the dispatcher reaches it; this shows the fetch is attacker-directed but not the deployment egress posture.
validation_plan.deployment: Ask the owner whether the production egress proxy denies RFC1918 and link-local destinations for the webhook dispatcher.
